note: Q1-F002. The SET is the authority; entry_count is telemetry. Added and removed are reported independently, so a repaired problem can never mask a new one. v2 SPLITS two things v1 conflated: the BASELINE measurement, which the Q1-F002 finding cites and which may never move, and the CURRENT census, which every later stage re-pins as it adds workflow steps. In v1 they were one field, so any stage that added a CI step could only go green by editing the number a prior finding had recorded — see Stage 5S finding 5S-F015.

baseline.why: cited by the Q1-F002 finding ledger as the measurement taken at that tag; a later stage may never rewrite it

lifecycle.active_phase: from Stage 5Q Q1 onward, repository-wide over every committed workflow
lifecycle.protected_surface: the current census of manually enumerated workflow steps that carry no committed universe query
lifecycle.next_phase_behaviour: every later stage that adds such a step RE-PINS `current` and leaves `baseline` untouched; a stage that cannot go green without editing `baseline` has found a defect in this gate rather than in itself
lifecycle.maintenance_behaviour: `current.gate_problems` is additive-or-shrinking and always re-derived from the real workflows; `baseline` is immutable and any change to it is a rewrite of recorded evidence
lifecycle.sunset_or_migration_condition: when every workflow step carries a committed universe query, at which point the census is empty and the anti-vacuity condition below fails loudly
lifecycle.anti_vacuity_condition: an empty pin is refused rather than matched against an empty census, and the live comparison must have examined a non-empty set of workflows
